function: Over-the-air aggregation of local model updates for differentially private FL: online design of transmit power scalar, artificial noise and active-RIS reflection pattern (pp. 3, 8-9).
system: K=10 single-antenna devices and one single-antenna server; active RIS with N=20 elements; uncoded AirComp uplink, block fading; frequency band not stated (pp. 3-4, 11).
method: Federated logistic regression with differential privacy over AirComp; RIS and power design by Lyapunov online optimization with SCA and SDR, not learned (pp. 4, 7-11).
data_channel: Own simulator: 3D geometry, distance path loss with exponents 3.8, 2.5, 2.2, Rayleigh small-scale fading; MNIST (60000 train, 10000 test) split over 10 devices (p. 11).
test_conditions: 1000 FL rounds; MNIST test set; same simulated channel setting; sweeps of privacy level, amplification power, and RIS size (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Same online policy with no RIS and passive RIS; active RIS with constant amplitude; no earlier published aggregation design simulated (pp. 10-12).
metrics: Training loss, test accuracy, accumulated disclosed-signal-to-effective-noise ratio (DSENR) against the privacy budget, effective noise power (pp. 11-12).
complexity: Worst-case O(UE(N+1)^4 sqrt(N+1) log2(1/o)(K+1)^3) for the RIS step; the power step is closed form (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 11: "all wireless channels suffer from Rayleigh fading"; path loss is a textbook power law [48], so this is a custom simulator, with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 13: "Fig. 7 shows the impact of the number of reflecting elements at RIS on the learning performance"; the paper sweeps privacy level, amplification power and RIS size, and never tests a trained model in a condition unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 11: "active RIS, FL system with passive RIS, and FL system" without RIS are compared; the passive and no-RIS cases reuse the paper's own algorithm (p. 10: "the same procedures in section IV-C"), and no earlier published aggregation design is simulated.
q4_support: p. 9: "the worst-case complexity of Algorithm" 1 is O(UE(N+1)^4 sqrt(N+1) log2(1/o)(K+1)^3) for the SCA and SDR steps; the power step is closed form.
q5_support: p. 11: "image classification task based on the well-known MNIST" dataset; MNIST is the dataset of the learning task only, the channel is simulated, and no code or data link is given.
notes: Area 7: over-the-air aggregation in AirComp FL with an active RIS (p. 3); it passes the learning check under the FL rule, since the learned element is the logistic regression trained across devices (p. 11). The RIS is active, with amplification (p. 4). The physical-layer design is optimization (Lyapunov, SCA, SDR), not learned (pp. 7-9). q3 is borderline: the passive-RIS case follows the earlier work [19] in idea, but it is solved by the paper's own algorithm (p. 10). q4 counts the complexity of the RIS design (p. 9). No carrier frequency is stated (Table III, p. 12).
